facts.subject: char:sera
facts.statement: Sera stood in the village square when the first new rain fell.

facts.subject: item:seed_case
facts.statement: Fenn returned the seed case to Sera.

facts.subject: char:sera
facts.speaker: char:sera
facts.statement: Sera released three seeds and closed the case on eight.

facts.subject: char:new_tree
facts.statement: A new sapling was alive beside the dead stump.

facts.subject: char:mael
facts.statement: The council recorded Mael’s resignation and named him former reeve.

facts.subject: item:memory_book
facts.statement: The village library took custody of the memory book.

facts.subject: char:orin
facts.statement: Orin returned to the orchard to hang a smaller bell.

facts.subject: item:bronze_bell
facts.statement: The old bronze bell remained in the village square.

facts.subject: char:sera
facts.statement: Sera recalled an apprenticeship with a travelling potter, though she could not remember when it began.
facts.note: Unknown date boundaries remain null. A remembered location never overwrites current narrated location; chapter-one past location ends before chapter one.

claims.speaker: char:mael
claims.content: I thought borrowing a memory was harmless.
claims.note: Only the speech act is confirmed; do not promote its content without separate evidence.

cognitions.content: Sera knew the new sapling was not the old tree restored.
cognitions.note: Confirmed that this character holds/held this epistemic attitude, not that a belief or suspicion is objectively true.

cognitions.content: Fenn had believed silence would protect the child’s name, but silence had protected Mael instead.
cognitions.note: Confirmed that this character holds/held this epistemic attitude, not that a belief or suspicion is objectively true.

cognitions.content: Sera could not know whether the distant cloud had been made by their seeds.
cognitions.note: Confirmed that this character holds/held this epistemic attitude, not that a belief or suspicion is objectively true.

cognitions.content: Orin believed the new sapling would need ordinary care as well as rain.
cognitions.note: Confirmed that this character holds/held this epistemic attitude, not that a belief or suspicion is objectively true.

cognitions.content: Fenn knows her silence protected Mael rather than the child’s name.
cognitions.note: Correction of the explicitly former belief, not an active continuation of it.

relations.statement: Sera trusted Orin to teach the next apprentice without concealing the cost.

hooks.statement: The ringing seed held Orin’s freely offered memory.
The warm page returned the memory Mael had taken.
The glove concealed the scar of the former keeper.
The child’s name belonged to the memory’s rightful giver.

mustNotRecord.statement: She intended to teach the next apprentice to keep a written account.
mustNotRecord.reason: An intention is not a completed event.

mustNotRecord.statement: If every gift remained voluntary, the orchard might never demand another debt.
mustNotRecord.reason: A conditional proposition is not an actual world state.

mustNotRecord.statement: She dreamed of a kitchen in which nobody had forgotten the door.
mustNotRecord.reason: Dream content is not waking canon.

uncertainties.statement: Sera could not know whether the distant cloud had been made by their seeds.
uncertainties.note: Retain uncertainty. Where no definite proposition is offered, recording only a suspects cognition or omitting a world fact is valid.
